intended_object: The canonical isomorphism of GL_n(k)-representations det^{λ_n} ⊗ 𝕊^μ(kⁿ) ≅ rationalWeylRep(λ), where μ is the polynomial part of the dominant weight λ. It identifies the usual tensor-product form of the rational Weyl module with the library's character-twist model (from the docstring and the module documentation).
explanation:
The construction is an equivalence of representations between two specific representations. The first is `detPowerRep k n λₙ ⊗ weylRepOfShape k n μ`, where `detPowerRep` is `ofLinearCharacter (det ^ m)` acting on k. The second is `rationalWeylRep k n λ`, which is defined as `charTwist (det ^ λₙ) (weylRepOfShape μ)` on the carrier of the Weyl module.

The underlying linear equivalence is `TensorProduct.lid : k ⊗ V ≃ V`, sending x ⊗ v to x • v. This is exactly the canonical map identifying the tensor product with a line on which g acts by det(g)^m with the scalar twist v ↦ det(g)^m · g·v. The equivariance proof follows from the library's general lemma `lid_ofLinearCharacter_tprod_apply`.

So it is the standard identification "det^m ⊗ V = V twisted by det^m", which is what the docstring claims. The setting (a commutative ring k with `Algebra ℚ k`, the group `GL (Fin n) k`) is inherited from the Weyl-module objects it relates, and the general version for an arbitrary linear character already exists in the library as `Representation.tprodEquivCharTwist`. Specializing it to these particular objects is appropriate and not too narrow. Mathlib has no direct counterpart.
